lines.text: Two payment screenshots from customers. One was edited. Nemotron reads both, and the ledger knows which is which.
Here's how. “I paid, here's my screenshot.” That's how customers write to a small online shop: a phone photo of their banking app, in Korean or Japanese.
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, on Nebius Token Factory, reads the photo. The payment, not the running total, not the ad, not the phone's clock.
Then the payment provider's ledger checks it: same amount, within ten minutes. And the money chain shows the one link where the money got stuck.
Another card alert. This one has its date edited.
Nemotron reads the edited date as written. It can't spot the edit. The ledger can: it has never seen that payment. The reply politely asks for the card statement, and nothing changes.
On sixteen held-out phone photos made by a separate agent, Nemotron read the payment and got the verdict right on fourteen. Free on-device OCR with payment rules: three.
Messages are messy too. Two addresses: the account is his wife's, but he paid with his own.
Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reads the message: who is writing, what they claim, which records to look up. Addresses are masked before the model sees them, and anything the message doesn't say is dropped.
A simple rule would grab the first address and find nothing.
A verifier, not the model, walks the chain. The order was saved under a typo, exmaple dot com, and the mail bounced.
Every call is on screen: which Nemotron did which job, the time, the tokens and the cost. Ultra is called only when the first reading is unsure.
Approve, and the fix runs. On the public demo, only your own copy of the data changes.
Ask for someone else's order, and it is not read. And when nothing was charged, it says so. Nothing is broken. You were never charged.

On twenty-two Korean and Japanese messages, Nemotron found who was writing in twenty; rules alone, sixteen. End to end, rules got one more right. One of Nemotron's misses was an attack where it named no sender, so nobody's records were read.
Paid, but nothing arrived? Here's the proof, found in one pass. NVIDIA Nemotron, on Nebius Token Factory.
